Proves that the actual primary birth region at a specified signed pitch index is exactly the finite union of closed actual nonbelt fine cells whose shifted pitch index equals it. The only scale assumptions are ℓ ≤ k and ℓ ≤ p. The origin, finite endpoint set, natural width and signed primary index are arbitrary; residues are in Fin (2^(p−ℓ)). Empty layers, non-retained identifiers, refinement depth zero, equal fine/pitch scales and disconnected primary regions are included. No new public region or index definition is introduced.

Section 11, prop:two-families, lines 212–218 and 299–323. The existing nonbelt-cell closure containment and exact fine-layer union are reused. The converse uses Euclidean signed quotient/remainder and closure into a finite closed union; it does not assert a union of whole half-open cells inside the open pitch interior.
